title: Minimal components give an isometric affinoid embedding
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $C\ne0$ be a reduced commutative unital affinoid $K$-algebra, meaning a quotient of a finite-variable Tate restricted-series algebra [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with its affinoid Banach topology. There are finitely many minimal prime ideals $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_s$ of $C$, with $s\ge1$, and these are all its minimal prime ideals; a minimal prime is a prime ideal containing no strictly smaller prime ideal. Each quotient $C_i=C/\mathfrak p_i$, with its quotient topology, is a nonzero affinoid integral domain, and the quotient maps $q_i:C\to C_i$ are continuous. For $H=C,C_i$ put $\sigma_H(h)=\sup_{\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Max}H}|h\bmod\mathfrak m|$, with the unique extending absolute values on the finite residue fields [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. The map $q:C\to\prod_{i=1}^s C_i$ is injective, and $\sigma_C(c)=\max_{1\le i\le s}\sigma_{C_i}(q_i(c))$ for every $c\in C$.

proof.text: Choose a quotient presentation $\alpha:T_r=K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle\twoheadrightarrow C$ inducing the given affinoid topology. Apply [lem-trf-tate-submodule-norm-controlled-generators] with free-module rank one to each ideal of $T_r$: every such ideal has finitely many generators. For an ideal $J\subset C$, generators of $\alpha^{-1}(J)$ map to generators of $J$, by lifting any element of $J$ and applying $\alpha$ to its generator expression. Thus every ideal of $C$ is finitely generated, so $C$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], its distinct minimal primes form a finite list $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_s$. This list is nonempty: since $C\ne0$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] gives a maximal ideal, and [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] with $I=0$ gives a minimal prime below it.

proof.text: For each $i$ put $J_i=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak p_i)\subset T_r$. This ideal is closed: for $f$ in its closure, the infimum of $\|f-h\|_G$ over $h\in J_i$ is zero; [lem-trf-tate-ideal-best-approximation] attains it, so $f=h\in J_i$. By [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion], $T_r$ is a complete normed commutative ring. Apply [lem-trf-closed-ideal-banach-quotient] to $T_r$ and $J_i$. It gives the complete quotient norm $N_i$ on $T_r/J_i$, with quotient topology and continuous open projection. The map $f+J_i\mapsto\alpha(f)+\mathfrak p_i$ is a bijective $K$-algebra homomorphism onto $C_i$: surjectivity is that of $\alpha$, and equality of the images means $f-g\in J_i$. Transport this norm and topology to $C_i$. The same closedness argument applies to $\ker\alpha$, and [lem-trf-closed-ideal-banach-quotient] applied to $T_r$ and $\ker\alpha$ shows that the topology of the quotient Gauss norm of $\alpha$, which is the given affinoid topology of $C$ [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], is the quotient topology of $\alpha$; step 3 uses this.

source.place: Section 1.3 Corollaries 9–10, printed pp.21–22; Section 1.4 Propositions 2 and 4, printed pp.22–23, and proof of Lemma 13, minimal-prime paragraph, printed p.27. Read online; local archival copy WANTED. Agent assembly using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: These transported topologies are exactly the requested quotient topologies. For any subset $U\subset C_i$, it is open for the topology of step 2 if and only if $(q_i\alpha)^{-1}(U)$ is open in $T_r$, if and only if $q_i^{-1}(U)$ is open in $C$, since the given topology of $C$ is the quotient topology of $\alpha$ (step 2). This is the definition of the quotient topology for $q_i$ and proves its continuity. The quotient is a Banach $K$-algebra: scalar multiplication by $a\ne0$ bijects the lifts of $x$ and $ax$ and scales their Gauss norms by $|a|$, giving $N_i(ax)=|a|N_i(x)$; the assertion for $a=0$ is immediate. Taking arbitrarily close lifts in the Gauss ultrametric inequality gives $N_i(x+y)\le\max(N_i(x),N_i(y))$. Completeness and submultiplicativity are step 2. The presentation $q_i\alpha$ makes it affinoid. Since $\mathfrak p_i$ is proper, $1+\mathfrak p_i\ne0$; since it is prime, a zero product of cosets has a zero factor. Hence $C_i$ is a nonzero integral domain.

proof.text: The map $q$ is a $K$-algebra homomorphism coordinatewise. Its kernel is $\bigcap_i\mathfrak p_i$, since its $i$th coordinate vanishes exactly on $\mathfrak p_i$. By [lem-per-nilradical-minimal-prime-intersection], this intersection is precisely the set of nilpotent elements of $C$. Reducedness means that every such element is zero. Therefore $\ker q=0$, and $q$ is injective: if $q(c)=q(d)$ then $c-d\in\ker q$ and $c=d$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], all residue fields and their unique extending absolute values defining $\sigma_C$ and $\sigma_{C_i}$ exist, and these suprema are finite nonnegative real numbers. Its contractivity assertion applied to $q_i:C\to C_i$ gives $\sigma_{C_i}(q_i(c))\le\sigma_C(c)$ for each $i$. Since $s\ge1$, their finite maximum $M$ exists and satisfies $M\le\sigma_C(c)$.

source.place: Section 1.3 Corollaries 9–10, printed pp.21–22; Section 1.4 Propositions 2 and 4, printed pp.22–23, and proof of Lemma 13, minimal-prime paragraph, printed p.27. Read online; local archival copy WANTED. Agent assembly using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Conversely, let $\mathfrak m$ be any maximal ideal of $C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] with $I=0$, it contains some $\mathfrak p_i$. The ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p_i\subset C_i$ is maximal: the map $C_i\to C/\mathfrak m$, $c+\mathfrak p_i\mapsto c+\mathfrak m$, is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak n$, so $C_i/\mathfrak n\cong C/\mathfrak m$ is a field. This is a $K$-isomorphism sending the residue of $q_i(c)$ to the residue of $c$. By uniqueness of the extending absolute values in [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], their values agree. Therefore $|c\bmod\mathfrak m|=|q_i(c)\bmod\mathfrak n|\le\sigma_{C_i}(q_i(c))\le M$. Taking the supremum over all $\mathfrak m$ gives $\sigma_C(c)\le M$. Together with step 5 this proves the asserted equality.
